holidays.name: National Awkward Moments Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace every cringe-worthy stumble, mistimed wave, and accidental 'you too' said to a waiter who told you to enjoy your meal. It encourages everyone to laugh at their own social blunders instead of replaying them at 3 a.m.
holidays.origin: Created as an unofficial observance in the early 2010s, popularized through social media and calendar-listing sites that celebrate human imperfection.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists call the intense embarrassment of remembering a past blunder 'cringe memory,' and nearly everyone experiences it regularly.

holidays.name: National Sloppy Joe Day
holidays.description: A salute to the gloriously messy sandwich of seasoned ground beef in a tangy tomato sauce piled onto a bun. Napkins are not optional; they are a survival strategy.
holidays.origin: The sandwich is often traced to early 20th-century America, with claims of origin in Sioux City, Iowa, around 1917, and a separate story tied to a Havana bar called Sloppy Joe's. The day itself is an unofficial food observance.
holidays.funFact: Sioux City's claim involves a cook named Joe who added tomato sauce to a loose-meat sandwich, while the Havana bar was reportedly a favorite hangout of Ernest Hemingway.

holidays.name: National Supermarket Employee Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the folks who restock the shelves, wrangle runaway carts, and tell you which aisle the capers are in. Cashiers, baggers, and stockers all get a well-earned round of applause.
holidays.origin: Established as an unofficial appreciation day recognizing the millions of workers in grocery stores, who became widely seen as essential workers in recent years.
holidays.funFact: The first self-service grocery store, Piggly Wiggly, opened in Memphis in 1916 and changed how people shopped by letting them pick items off the shelves themselves.

holidays.name: Awkward Moments Day Companion: Forgive Mom and Dad Day
holidays.description: A gentle observance inviting people to let go of old family grudges, from the time someone cut your hair into a bowl shape to that unforgettable road trip fight about directions.
holidays.origin: An informal awareness day in the same spirit as other family-themed calendar observances, promoted by greeting-card and lifestyle sites as a day for reconciliation.
holidays.funFact: Studies on forgiveness suggest that letting go of grudges is associated with lower stress levels and better sleep.

holidays.name: Annual Biodiesel Day
holidays.description: A nerdy and surprisingly eco-friendly celebration of fuel made from vegetable oils, animal fats, and recycled restaurant grease. Yes, your french fry oil might one day power a truck.
holidays.origin: Celebrated around the globe to recognize the work of Rudolf Diesel, who ran an early engine on peanut oil, and to promote renewable fuel alternatives.
holidays.funFact: Rudolf Diesel demonstrated one of his engines running on peanut oil at the 1900 World's Fair in Paris.
